draft.title: How fossils form
card: A fossil is the preserved remains or traces of a living thing from long ago. Traces include footprints, burrows and droppings.
Fossils usually start when a dead organism is buried quickly in sediment, such as mud or sand. Burial protects it from being eaten or broken down.
Over a very long time, the sediment hardens into sedimentary rock. Water carrying minerals seeps into hard parts such as bones and shells, and the minerals slowly replace them.
Different layers of rock hold different fossils. This shows that different organisms lived at different times.
draft.remember: Quick burial, then minerals slowly replace the hard parts, leaving a fossil.

a.q: Why does a dead fish buried quickly in mud have a better chance of becoming a fossil than one left on the lakebed?
opts: Burial protects it from being eaten or broken down
Burial turns the fish into rock straight away
Mud adds new bones to the fish as it is buried
Burial makes the fish older than other organisms
a.why: Sediment covers the remains, so scavengers and decay cannot destroy them. Burial does not change the fish into rock at once, because minerals replace the hard parts slowly over a very long time.
a.clue: Think about what could happen to the fish if it stayed uncovered.

b.q: A student in Broken Hill finds a rock containing a shell shape made of stone. Which statement best explains how the shell became a fossil?
opts: Buried in sediment, its shell was slowly replaced by minerals
The shell melted and cooled into stone as magma
The shell was squashed flat by heat and became new rock
The shell turned to stone soon after the animal died
b.why: The shell was buried in sediment, and minerals carried by water slowly replaced its hard parts. The shell turning to stone soon after death is wrong because the change takes a very long time.
b.clue: Fossils form slowly, and burial comes first.
